Nine places to go deeper than this lesson, or to check a citation yourself before it goes
into a real Lakeshore document. All nine were checked and loading at the time this page was
written.

- **[21 U.S.C. 374, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/21/374)**
  — the full statutory section this lesson excerpted from. This lesson only quotes (a)(1),
  (b)(1), (c), and (h)(1)'s opening clause; the full section is long and heavily amended, and
  worth skimming once to see how much of it this lesson deliberately left out (infant-formula
  and clinical-study-inspection provisions, among others).

- **[FDA, Inspection Observations](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/inspection-references/inspection-observations)**
  — FDA's own public page describing Form FDA 483, including where FDA publishes
  spreadsheets summarizing what gets cited on 483s by fiscal year. Useful for seeing what
  kinds of observations are common across FDA's regulated industries generally.

- **[FDA, "CDER GCP Inspections and Outcomes" (PDF)](https://www.fda.gov/media/164382/download)**
  — the source for this lesson's NAI/VAI/OAI classification quotes. **Read this one with the
  scope caveat in mind**: it's a presentation specifically about Good Clinical Practice (GCP)
  inspections of clinical drug trials, not about CGMP inspections of a manufacturing or
  blood-collection facility. Only its general three-outcome classification scheme (NAI, VAI,
  OAI) applies beyond that context — its clinical-trial-specific examples and statistics do
  not.

- **[Understanding FDA Inspections and Data](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y-qkNfMze9c)**
  (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this
  lesson: FDA's own 2023 webinar on how CGMP inspections work, what a 483 is and is not, and how
  FDA reviews inspectional findings. It is drug-manufacturing-focused, so treat its examples as
  context, not as blood-establishment rules. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA, Understanding FDA Inspections and Data (event page and slides)](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/understanding-fda-inspections-and-data-09062023)**
  — the FDA event page for that webinar, listing its speakers and the downloadable slide deck
  (including a section on understanding CGMP inspections and 483s). Read the slides when you want
  the same material faster than the video, with the same drug-manufacturing scope. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA, Form 483 Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/inspection-references/fda-form-483-frequently-asked-questions)**
  — FDA's own plain-language Q&A on the 483, including that it is not a final Agency
  determination and that it is considered together with the Establishment Inspection Report,
  on-site evidence, and the company's response. Read it before briefing your QA on what a 483
  does and doesn't mean. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA, Investigations Operations Manual](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/inspection-references/investigations-operations-manual)**
  — the internal reference FDA investigators and field staff work from, published so regulated
  industry can understand FDA operations. Chapter 5 covers inspections. Skim it to see the
  investigator's side of the process this lesson describes from Lakeshore's side. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA, Inspection Classification Database](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/inspection-references/inspection-classification-database)**
  — FDA's page on how it shares inspection classification information with the public, pointing
  to the FDA Data Dashboard and the database's FAQs. Useful for seeing that NAI, VAI, and OAI are
  real, published classifications rather than just slide vocabulary. Verified loading via `curl`
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA, Inspections Yield Valuable Results, Regardless of Classification](https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/regulatory-news-stories-and-features/inspections-yield-valuable-results-regardless-classification)**
  — an FDA feature explaining how the Establishment Inspection Report can serve as an
  educational tool for firms and why inspections matter even when no violations are found. Read
  it for FDA's own framing of what a well-run inspection looks like from the firm's side.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
